title: Coefficient square for normalized relative cyclic rows
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site in a universe containing all parameter sets [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Use internal $R$-modules $\mathcal M_R$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and action categories $\mathcal A_P(R)$ for the condensed group $\underline P(S)=C(S,P)$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $G,H$ be profinite groups, $u:\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}\to H$ a continuous homomorphism and $\tau=u(1)$. Write $L_J^G$ for trivial-$J$ inflation and $\Gamma_J^G$ for its invariant-inclusion-normalized right adjoint, retaining $G$, for $J=H,\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$. Let $V=\operatorname{Res}_{1_G\times u}$, $U_J:\mathcal A_{G\times J}(R)\to\mathcal A_J(R)$ and $U_0:\mathcal A_G(R)\to\mathcal M_R$ forget $G$. Write $Q$ for ordinary derived localization and $\alpha^G_{J,P}:Q\Gamma_J^G P\to R\Gamma_J^G(QP)$ for its canonical computation unit on bounded-below complexes. For a bounded-below $G\times\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$-complex $N$, let $K^G(N)^n=N^n\oplus N^{n-1}$, with $d(x,y)=(d_Nx,(T-1)x-d_Ny)$, where $T$ is the action of $1\in\mathbf Z$, and let $b_N:\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G N\to K^G(N)$ be $(\mathrm{inclusion},0)$. Use the mate $\beta^G$ of [lem-sfb-relative-restriction-mate-forgetting] and the cyclic comparison $\lambda^G=(\theta^G)^{-1}$ characterized on every bounded-below complex by $\theta^G\alpha^G_{\mathbf Z}=Qb$, as in [lem-sfb-cyclic-row-derived-comparison]. Let $\varphi:R\to R'$ be any condensed ring map, with no flatness hypothesis. Write $s_{G\times J},s_G$ for scalar restriction. The commuting scalar/projection square of action ringed topoi gives canonical isomorphisms
$$d_J:R\Gamma_J^{G,R}D(s_{G\times J})\xrightarrow{\sim}D(s_G)R\Gamma_J^{G,R'}.$$
They are the adjunction-normalized right-derived composition comparisons. The inverse $d_J^{-1}$ is the mate of the identity between the two composites of inflation and scalar restriction. For any bounded-below $G\times J$-complexes $N$ over $R$ and $N'$ over $R'$, and any derived coefficient morphism $f:QN\to D(s_{G\times J})(QN')$, the induced coefficient map is $d_JR\Gamma_J^{G,R}(f)$. The actual $\beta^G$ squares commute, and so do the squares with the normalized forgetting comparisons $\delta_J$.

For every bounded-below injective resolution $N'\to I'$ over $R'$, the scalar-restricted cyclic augmentation $b_{sI'}$ is a quasi-isomorphism, even when $sI'$ is not termwise injective over $R$. On this model the identities are
$$K_R^G(sI')=s_GK_{R'}^G(I'),\qquad d_{\mathbf Z}\alpha_R(sI')=s_G\alpha_{R'}(I'),$$
and $\alpha_R(sI')$ is invertible. Under this total identification,
$$s_G\lambda^G_{R'}=d_{\mathbf Z}\lambda^G_R.$$
Together with naturality this gives the coefficient squares for arbitrary $f$ and for $c=(\lambda^G)^{-1}\beta^G$. All these identifications commute with canonical shifts and triangle boundaries. Scalar restriction is exact, but ordinary scalar extension need not be exact, and preservation of injectives by $s$ is not part of the assertion.

proof.text: Present the action categories by the small action sites of [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction], using the projection of group sheaves $G\times J\to G$, including $J=\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$. Its module inverse image is trivial-$J$ inflation: its right adjoint is precisely $\Gamma_J^G$, since the adjunction transpose restricts the codomain to the fixed submodule, as specified in [lem-sfb-product-action-exact-forgetting]. A coefficient map defines an identity-underlying ringed-topos morphism, whose module direct image is scalar restriction. This functor is exact: its kernels and sheafified cokernels have the unchanged underlying abelian sheaves. Thus its ordinary derived functor is termwise scalar restriction. The square of the coefficient morphisms and the projection has the literal identity geometric comparison and compatible structural ring maps; no tensor-exactness is needed.

proof.text:
Use the normalized ringed-derived comparisons, not an assertion that restriction preserves injectives. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to the two equal paths $(B_{G\times J},R')\to(B_G,R)$ in step 1, and its specified geometric 2-isomorphism comparison. This gives $d_J:R\Gamma_J^{G,R}D(s_{G\times J})\simeq D(s_G)R\Gamma_J^{G,R'}$. The right-derived-unit formulas in [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-composition-comparison, lem-sfb-ringed-derived-two-iso-comparison] give, on every bounded-below $P'$, the equation
$$d_{J,QP'}\alpha^R_{J,sP'}=s_G\alpha^{R'}_{J,P'}.$$
Indeed the underived path comparison is the identity on the fixed-section subsheaf, and the computation units for the exact scalar functors are identities. Adjunction compatibility identifies $d_J^{-1}$ with the mixed mate of $L_J^R s_G=s_{G\times J}L_J^{R'}$: its transpose is $L_J^R s_GR\Gamma_J^{R'}\to s_{G\times J}L_J^{R'}R\Gamma_J^{R'}\xrightarrow{s\varepsilon'}s_{G\times J}$. This also fixes the normalization on arbitrary complexes.

proof.text:
The actual $\beta^G$ is the mate specified in [lem-sfb-relative-restriction-mate-forgetting]. For $X=R\Gamma_H^{G,R}N$ and $f:N\to sN'$, compare the two coefficient/restriction paths to $s_GR\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^{G,R'}V'N'$. Transpose using $L_{\mathbf Z}^R\dashv R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^R$ and the mixed comparison of step 2. Both transposes are
$$L_{\mathbf Z}^R X=V L_H^R X\xrightarrow{V\varepsilon^R_{H,N}}VN\xrightarrow{Vf}VsN'=sV'N'.$$
The equality follows by substituting the mate formula and cancelling adjacent unit/counit pairs with the two adjunction triangle identities; naturality moves $f$ past each counit. Bijectivity of transposition proves the coefficient square as an equality of derived arrows. With $V$ replaced by forgetting $G$, the identical calculation proves compatibility with $\delta_J$: its adjunction normalization is the identical fixed-section inclusion by [lem-sfb-relative-restriction-mate-forgetting]. Literal commutation of scalar restriction and forgetting supplies the other sides. Thus the normalized forgetting square commutes as well. To check the unit normalization of the forgetting square on a possibly noninjective complex $P$, resolve $P\to J$ over $R$. Naturality and the normalization on injective $J$ show $\delta\,U_0\alpha_P=\alpha_{U_JP}$ after postcomposition by the invertible derived image of $P\to J$, hence before postcomposition. Evaluate the coefficient/forgetting square on $R'$-injective $I'$ and precompose by $U_0\alpha_R(sI')$. This is invertible by step 4. Both paths become the identical scalar-restricted computation unit, by the preceding equation and step 2 (also for the projection to the trivial group). Cancel and extend by resolutions and naturality.

proof.text:
For a bounded-below $R'$-injective complex $I'$, [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] makes $\alpha^{R'}_{J,I'}$ invertible. The equation of step 2 and invertibility of $d_J$ imply that $\alpha^R_{J,sI'}$ is invertible. This is a computation-unit argument and does not assert that the terms of $sI'$ are injective. In the cyclic case, scalar restriction changes neither the biproduct coordinates nor $T-1$. Hence literally
$$K_R^G(sI')=s_GK_{R'}^G(I'),\qquad b^R_{sI'}=s_G b^{R'}_{I'}.$$
The second identity uses the identical fixed-section subsheaves in the domain. The augmentation $b^{R'}_{I'}$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-sfb-cyclic-row-derived-comparison]. Exactness of scalar restriction therefore proves the asserted quasi-isomorphism for $b^R_{sI'}$. This argument works for any such injective complex, hence every resolution in the question.

proof.text:
Write $\theta_R=\lambda_R^{-1}$. On $I'$ the defining equations from [lem-sfb-cyclic-row-derived-comparison] and step 2 give
$$s_G\theta_{R'}\,d_{\mathbf Z}\,\alpha_R(sI')=s_G\theta_{R'}\,s_G\alpha_{R'}(I')=s_GQb_{I'}=Qb_{sI'}=\theta_R\alpha_R(sI').$$
Cancel the invertible $\alpha_R(sI')$ from step 4. Thus $s_G\theta_{R'}d_{\mathbf Z}=\theta_R$, or, after inverting the row comparisons, $s_G\lambda_{R'}=d_{\mathbf Z}\lambda_R$ under the displayed total identification. Every bounded-below object over $R'$ admits an injective resolution by the bounded-below derived construction of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]; naturality along its invertible localization extends the equality from $I'$ to that object. No uniqueness from degree zero alone is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), auxiliary relative cyclic coefficient calculation; agent argument.

proof.text:
For arbitrary derived $f:QN\to D(s)(QN')$, naturality of $\lambda_R$ gives
$$\lambda_R(sQN')\,QK_R(f)=R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^{G,R}(f)\,\lambda_R(QN).$$
Postcompose with $d_{\mathbf Z}$ and substitute step 5. The result is precisely the coefficient square for $\lambda$, with coefficient map $d_{\mathbf Z}R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^{G,R}(f)$. Composing its inverse square with the $\beta$ square of step 3 proves the square for $c=\lambda^{-1}\beta$. This uses functoriality on derived arrows, not merely maps between chosen chain models.

proof.text:
Check the coefficient comparison's shifts directly on models. For an $R'$-injective bounded-below complex $I'$, choose an $R$-injective resolution $a:sI'\to J$. The computation of [lem-sp-kinjective-computes] and naturality of computation units represent $\alpha_R(sI')$ by $Q\Gamma_J^G(a)$ under the injective computation at $J$. This is invertible by step 4, so $d_J$ is represented by its inverse, under the injective computation of $s_GR\Gamma_J^{G,R'}(QI')$ by $Qs_G\Gamma_J^{G,R'}I'$. For a shift $n$, use the shifted resolutions $I'[n],J[n],a[n]$: they are K-injective resolutions by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift], and termwise additive invariants give $\Gamma_J^G(a[n])=\Gamma_J^G(a)[n]$ under canonical shifts. Taking inverses proves the shift equation for $d_J$, and naturality extends it to all bounded-below objects. Naturality applied to a triangle's last arrow, together with that shift equation, gives its boundary square.

The $\beta,\delta$ and row comparisons preserve shifts and boundaries by [lem-sfb-relative-restriction-mate-forgetting, lem-sfb-cyclic-row-derived-comparison]. Scalar restriction leaves the signed shift $(x,y)\mapsto(x,(-1)^n y)$ and cone reordering of [lem-sfb-cyclic-total-triangulated] unchanged. Thus compositions and inverses in the preceding coefficient equations preserve the boundary squares as well. No equality is detected by conservative forgetting. Ordinary scalar extension is unused: $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z/2$ sends the injection $\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{2}\mathbf Z$ to zero.
